title: Blinded data, non-tomographic
summary: At the fiducial cuts (12′–83′, 300 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1600) ξ₋ᴮ and Cℓ BB fail; the other B-mode nulls pass.
banner: Blinded (blind: unions): E-mode data vectors are concealed; do not interpret cosmology
provenance: ShapePipe SP v2.0, upper bound 9 on galaxy size relative to the PSF; 170.6M galaxies on 20,515 of the 22,901 tiles in the v2.0.0 release, 4,690 deg²
for the covariance only: the sum of the four bins of the first working DR6 BPZ+SOM n(z), not the recalibrated n(z) of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468
sp_validation run/tomo1101 @ 7081c2d0 (measured 1 Nov); figures rendered 10 Nov with feat/page-figures-2d @ 489e3f3c (catalogue-level panels: run/dashboard-tomo1101 @ 54220f69)
headline_note: PTE of each B-mode null test at the fiducial cuts (12′–83′, 300 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1600)

tables.caption: Probability to exceed the χ² of each B-mode data vector against zero, with the analytic covariance.

figures.caption: Blinded shear correlation functions ξ₊ and ξ₋, multiplied by θ, in 20 logarithmic bins from 1′ to 250′. Error bars are from the analytic covariance.
figures.alt: Blinded shear correlation functions ξ₊ and ξ₋, multiplied by θ, in 20 logarithmic bins from 1′ to 250′. Error bars are from the analytic covariance.

figures.caption: Blinded E-mode angular power spectrum C_ℓ^EE, multiplied by ℓ: NaMaster pseudo-Cℓ, corrected for the survey mask. Error bars are from the Gaussian covariance. Shading marks bands outside the fiducial 300 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1600.
figures.alt: Blinded E-mode angular power spectrum C_ℓ^EE, multiplied by ℓ: NaMaster pseudo-Cℓ, corrected for the survey mask. Error bars are from the Gaussian covariance. Shading marks bands outside the fiducial 300 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1600.

figures.caption: Blinded ξ± (black) split into pure E modes (blue), pure B modes (red) and ambiguous modes that cannot be assigned to either (grey), all multiplied by θ. Lensing makes no B modes, so they are a null test. Shading marks scales outside the fiducial 12′–83′; the vertical range is set by the points inside it.
figures.alt: Blinded ξ± (black) split into pure E modes (blue), pure B modes (red) and ambiguous modes that cannot be assigned to either (grey), all multiplied by θ. Lensing makes no B modes, so they are a null test. Shading marks scales outside the fiducial 12′–83′; the vertical range is set by the points inside it.

figures.caption: B-mode COSEBIs Bₙ (complete orthogonal sets of E/B-integrals, a compact E/B split of ξ±) in units of their uncertainty, over the fiducial 12′–83′ (filled) and the full 1′–250′ (open). The headline null test uses n ≤ 6; higher modes are shaded.
figures.alt: B-mode COSEBIs Bₙ (complete orthogonal sets of E/B-integrals, a compact E/B split of ξ±) in units of their uncertainty, over the fiducial 12′–83′ (filled) and the full 1′–250′ (open). The headline null test uses n ≤ 6; higher modes are shaded.

figures.caption: Pseudo-Cℓ B-mode (BB) and E×B (EB) power spectra in units of their uncertainty; lensing makes neither. Shading marks bands outside 300 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1600.
figures.alt: Pseudo-Cℓ B-mode (BB) and E×B (EB) power spectra in units of their uncertainty; lensing makes neither. Shading marks bands outside 300 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1600.

figures.caption: Probability to exceed (PTE) the χ² of the B modes against zero, for every choice of smallest and largest scale on the 20-bin grid: pure-mode ξ₊ᴮ, pure-mode ξ₋ᴮ and COSEBIs Bₙ with n ≤ 6. Saturated colours mark PTE below 0.05 or above 0.95; the fiducial cut is outlined.
figures.alt: Probability to exceed (PTE) the χ² of the B modes against zero, for every choice of smallest and largest scale on the 20-bin grid: pure-mode ξ₊ᴮ, pure-mode ξ₋ᴮ and COSEBIs Bₙ with n ≤ 6. Saturated colours mark PTE below 0.05 or above 0.95; the fiducial cut is outlined.

figures.caption: PTE of the Cℓ BB χ² against zero for every choice of lowest and highest band; the fiducial 300 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1600 is outlined.

figures.caption: Residuals of PSF validation stars against the PSF model at their positions: ellipticity (Δe), fourth-order moments (ΔM⁽⁴⁾) and size, as √(T★/T_PSF) − 1 with T the second-moment size. Means and σ use every finite detection.
figures.alt: Residuals of PSF validation stars against the PSF model at their positions: ellipticity (Δe), fourth-order moments (ΔM⁽⁴⁾) and size, as √(T★/T_PSF) − 1 with T the second-moment size. Means and σ use every finite detection.

figures.caption: Galaxy–PSF cross-correlations τ₂,₊ and τ₅,₊, multiplied by θ, for the catalogue without leakage correction. The band is the 68% range of the α, β, η leakage model of the raw catalogue over coefficient-resampling draws. Error bars are from the analytic τ covariance; points whose variance is not positive have none.
figures.alt: Galaxy–PSF cross-correlations τ₂,₊ and τ₅,₊, multiplied by θ, for the catalogue without leakage correction. The band is the 68% range of the α, β, η leakage model of the raw catalogue over coefficient-resampling draws. Error bars are from the analytic τ covariance; points whose variance is not positive have none.

figures.caption: Galaxy–PSF cross-correlations τ₀, τ₂ and τ₅, fitted by the PSF leakage model with coefficients α (leakage), β (ellipticity residual) and η (size residual). The band is the model's 68% range over coefficient-resampling draws.
figures.alt: Galaxy–PSF cross-correlations τ₀, τ₂ and τ₅, fitted by the PSF leakage model with coefficients α (leakage), β (ellipticity residual) and η (size residual). The band is the model's 68% range over coefficient-resampling draws.

figures.caption: Coefficient-resampling draws of the leakage parameters (68 and 95% contours), not Bayesian samples. Axes omit 0.3% of each marginal tail. Full sample ranges: α [-0.0247, 0.041]; β [0.938, 1.61]; η [-4.01, 4.74]. Displayed η range: [-2.78, 3.57].
figures.alt: Coefficient-resampling draws of the leakage parameters (68 and 95% contours), not Bayesian samples. Axes omit 0.3% of each marginal tail. Full sample ranges: α [-0.0247, 0.041]; β [0.938, 1.61]; η [-4.01, 4.74]. Displayed η range: [-2.78, 3.57].

figures.caption: Every estimate of the PSF leakage coefficient. Object-wise: regressions of galaxy on PSF ellipticity per component (a₁₁, a₂₂) and their mean. Scale-dependent α(θ) = τ₀,₊/ρ₀,₊: its weighted mean, the intercept of a linear fit in θ, and its value at the smallest θ. ρ/τ fit: α of the leakage model.

figures.caption: ρ statistics: auto- and cross-correlations of the PSF-model ellipticity and of the star-minus-model residuals in ellipticity (ρ₀–ρ₂) and in size-weighted ellipticity (ρ₃–ρ₅). Absolute values; open markers are negative.
figures.alt: ρ statistics: auto- and cross-correlations of the PSF-model ellipticity and of the star-minus-model residuals in ellipticity (ρ₀–ρ₂) and in size-weighted ellipticity (ρ₃–ρ₅). Absolute values; open markers are negative.

figures.caption: PSF leakage α₁, α₂ from weighted regressions of calibrated galaxy ellipticity on the PSF-model ellipticity at each galaxy, without object-wise leakage correction, in eight equal-count bins of resolution each split into eight equal-count bins of signal-to-noise. Hatched cells have |α| < 2σ, with σ the fit uncertainty.
figures.alt: PSF leakage α₁, α₂ from weighted regressions of calibrated galaxy ellipticity on the PSF-model ellipticity at each galaxy, without object-wise leakage correction, in eight equal-count bins of resolution each split into eight equal-count bins of signal-to-noise. figures.caption: Change of the weighted mean calibrated ellipticity per standard deviation of each galaxy or PSF property (left), and that slope over its fit uncertainty (right). Slopes are fits to the means in 20 bins of each property, with shape-noise errors that omit spatially correlated noise, which matters most for RA and Dec. Galaxy size is √T; the size ratio is T/T_PSF.
figures.alt: Change of the weighted mean calibrated ellipticity per standard deviation of each galaxy or PSF property (left), and that slope over its fit uncertainty (right). figures.caption: Scale-dependent PSF leakage α(θ) = τ₀,₊/ρ₀,₊ for all galaxies and in tertiles of galaxy r magnitude, with jackknife errors. Each bin is calibrated with its own shear response plus the global selection response; the faint bin's selection response is larger, so its |α| is likely underestimated by about 10–20%.
